title: Noahic Covenant
summary:
God speaks to Noah and his sons, establishing a covenant that reaches beyond their own family. It includes their descendants and every living creature that came from the ark: birds, livestock, and wild animals. The promise is that floodwaters will never again destroy all flesh or devastate the earth in this way.

God appoints the rainbow in the clouds as the covenant's visible sign. When clouds gather and the rainbow appears, God says he will remember the promise between himself and all living creatures. The declaration is repeated to emphasize that this is an enduring covenant for future generations. The passage closes by identifying the rainbow once more as the sign of the promise established with all life on earth.

title: Abrahamic Covenant
summary:
God calls Abram to leave his country, relatives, and father's household for a land he will be shown. The promise includes becoming a great nation, receiving a great name, and bringing blessing to all the earth's families.

In a later vision, Abram questions what God's gifts can mean while he remains childless. God promises an heir from his own body and descendants as numerous as the stars. Abram believes, and God counts that trust as righteousness. When Abram asks about possessing the land, he is told to prepare animals and divide them.

As darkness falls, Abram hears that his descendants will suffer in a foreign land before leaving with wealth and eventually returning. A smoking furnace and flaming torch pass between the divided animals. God promises his descendants a territory stretching from the river of Egypt to the Euphrates.

When Abram is ninety-nine, God renews the covenant and changes his name to Abraham. Nations and kings will descend from him, and Canaan is promised to his descendants. Circumcision, removal of the foreskin, becomes the required bodily sign for males in his household and later generations. It includes those born in the household and those bought as slaves. The passage ends with exclusion from the people for a male who remains uncircumcised.

title: Sinai / Mosaic Covenant
summary:
At the mountain, God tells Moses to remind Israel how he acted against Egypt and carried the people to himself as on eagles' wings. If they obey his voice and keep the covenant, they will be his special possession among the peoples. They are called to be a kingdom of priests and a holy nation.

In the later covenant ceremony, Moses reports God's words and rulings, and the people promise to obey. He writes the words down and builds an altar with twelve pillars representing Israel's tribes. Young men offer sacrifices, and Moses puts half the blood in basins while sprinkling the other half on the altar.

He reads the covenant book aloud, and the people repeat their commitment to obedience. Moses then sprinkles blood on them, identifying it as the blood of the covenant God has made with them concerning these words. The people have now heard the terms, promised obedience, and received the blood that marks the covenant.

title: Priestly Covenant with Phinehas
summary:
Phinehas, the grandson of Aaron, rises from the gathered community with a spear. He follows an Israelite man into a shelter and kills both the man and the woman with him. The account states that the plague among the Israelites then stops, after twenty-four thousand deaths.

God tells Moses that Phinehas has turned away divine anger by acting with God's own jealousy. Because of this, God grants him a covenant of peace. The promise extends to his descendants as an enduring priesthood. The passage describes his action as making atonement for Israel, turning aside the judgment against the community. It ends with the divine declaration of that priestly promise.

title: Davidic Covenant
summary:
God sends Nathan to remind David of his rise from shepherding to ruling Israel. The message credits God with accompanying him and defeating his enemies. It promises David a great name and Israel a secure place to live, with relief from oppression and war. God also promises to establish David's house, meaning his royal line.

After David's death, a descendant will succeed him and build a house for God's name. God will relate to this ruler as a father to a son. Wrongdoing will bring discipline, but divine loyalty will not be withdrawn as it was from Saul. The promise closes with David's house, kingdom, and throne established forever. Nathan delivers the whole message to David.

The selected verses from Psalm 89 recall the same commitment in the language of covenant and oath. God declares that David's descendants and throne will be established across generations.

title: New Covenant
summary:
Jeremiah announces a future covenant with Israel and Judah that will differ from the covenant made when their ancestors left Egypt. That earlier covenant was broken. In the promised relationship, God will place his law within the people and write it on their hearts. All will know him, from the least to the greatest, and he will forgive their wrongdoing.

The selected verse from Luke presents Jesus taking the cup after supper. He identifies it with the new covenant in his blood, poured out for his followers.

Hebrews describes a superior ministry and a better covenant founded on better promises. It quotes Jeremiah's announcement at length, emphasizing inward knowledge of God's law, belonging to God, and forgiveness. The passage argues that speaking of a new covenant makes the first one old and near disappearance.

title: Aaronic Blessing
summary:
God instructs Moses to give Aaron and his sons the words they are to use when blessing Israel. The blessing asks for God's protection, gracious attention, and peace. It describes that attention through the image of God's face shining upon the people and turning toward them.

The closing instruction explains the relationship between the priests' words and God's action. By speaking this blessing, Aaron and his sons place God's name upon the Israelites. God then promises to bless them. The priests are given the words to speak, while God identifies himself as the one who grants the blessing.
